children.text: The titration of a weak acid with a strong base (or a weak base with a strong acid) is somewhat more complicated than a strong acid-strong base titration, but it follows the same general principles. When a weak acid is titrated with a strong base, the strong acid and strong base react completely until one of the species is used up, and the remaining substances then reach equilibrium. The pH depends on the relative amounts of the species in the solution at that point. To understand the pH calculations, it can be useful to consider the titration as having four phases.
